title: Lightweight sidecar OTLP probe for lossy mobile clients with granular retry policy
creator: Aisha Grant
description: Implement a compact sidecar process to run alongside mobile/web SDKs in edge hosts and mobile gateways. The sidecar will accept intermittent OTLP/HTTP and gRPC payloads from lossy clients, perform lightweight envelope normalization, local buffering (in-memory only), and an adaptive retry/backoff strategy tuned for cellular and spotty networks. Goals: minimize client retransmit logic, reduce duplicate-span ingestion, expose export-level metrics for latency/drop rate, and provide safe failure modes that avoid blocking application requests.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar binary < 30MB compressed and < 40MB resident in low-end edge containers
Accepts OTLP/HTTP and OTLP/gRPC from SDKs with 1:1 passthrough of attributes unless redaction rules apply
Adaptive retry policy that uses network-quality hint + exponentially decaying backoff with jitter
In-memory ring buffer with configurable limits and LRU drop on overflow; no disk writes
Prometheus /metrics endpoint with export_latency_seconds histogram, export_retries_total, export_dropped_spans_total
Canary rollout demonstrates p99 export latency < 2s for 95% of traffic and dropped span rate < 1% under simulated poor network
Graceful fallback: when sidecar overloaded, SDKs should receive HTTP 202 and continue (no blocking), and traces should be marked with sidecar_delivery=best_effort
design_notes: 2026-03-02: Spike compared two architectures: in-process SDK helper vs independent sidecar. Chosen sidecar for language-agnostic deployment and easier memory isolation.
Protocol: prefer OTLP/gRPC for non-browser clients; OTLP/HTTP/JSON accepted for browser/mobile proxies. Convert both to canonical OTLP proto before export.
Sampling: sidecar will not change sampling decisions but will attach a provisional local-sampled flag when it drops spans to aid post-hoc analysis.
Deduplication: keep short-lived 8k LRU cache keyed by (traceid, spanid, client_nonce) to reduce duplicate ingestion from retries.
Security: mutual TLS optional for gateway deployments; support token passthrough for hosted ingest. No persistent secret storage; tokens provided via environment or mounted Kubernetes secret volumes.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope normalization + header translation
Integration tests: run SDK -> sidecar -> mock-tempo/tempo-stub verifying headers and span shapes
Chaos test: simulate 50% packet loss and ensure retry/backoff reduces client retransmits and maintain drop rate <1%
Load test: 2000 RPS small-spans to verify memory and latency under pressure
E2E canary: deploy to 5% of mobile gateway instances with detailed dashboarding
implementation_notes: Language: Rust (chosen for small binary size and memory guarantees). Prototype exists in /confluence/observability-edge/sidecar-proto (link in PR).
Buffer: ring buffer with configurable soft and hard limits; soft limit triggers aggressive backpressure to clients via 429/202 mappings
Export: use existing OTLP relay logic from ENG-421999 with export retries abstracted into a shared library
Metrics: expose prometheus metrics and a lightweight /healthz + /debug/queue endpoints for ops
Observability: ship traces of the sidecar itself to 'redwood-internal/sidecar' dataset for SLO tracking

risks: Mobile proxies may not send client hints needed for adaptive backoff; fallback heuristics required
Deduplication cache could increase memory under pathological trace churn; need watchdog and metrics
Misconfiguration could cause increased visible drop rate — require safe defaults and feature flag gating during rollout
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dogfood on staging cluster with synthetic mobile traffic
Stage 1: Canary 5% of mobile gateway hosts (feature-flagged) for 72 hours
Stage 2: Increment to 25% if SLOs met; monitor export_latency_seconds and export_dropped_spans_total
Stage 3: Full rollout after 2 weeks with rollback playbook prepared
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: Sidecar - Export Latency & Drops (by client_version, region, gateway)
Alert: export_dropped_spans_total > 0.5% over 15m for high-volume clients -> P1
Runbook: include steps to flip feature flag, disable sidecar autoscaling, and fallback SDK policy
